note: Built as ballot/lean/mn_endorsements.json is. Each record is one line of one party page, matched to one race and one candidate on the lists already loaded in ballot_local_2026.sqlite (office, place and name all fit, one fit only). Wyoming has four parties on the 2026 November ballot for state and county offices (Republican, Democratic, Libertarian, Constitution); 'Independent' is not a party. No page read for this file calls anything an endorsement for a 2026 state or local race, so 'endorsements' is empty. Under 'other_support', with the page's own wording in 'kind' and never to be shown as an endorsement: the Wyoming Democratic Party's '2026 Candidates' (two pages: every card's name, office terms and counties; the cards' e-mail, blurbs and links were not read), the Albany County Democratic Party's '2026 Local Candidates' and '2026 State Candidates' (only each section heading and the name under it were read; the sections carry contact details), and the Constitution Party National Committee's 'Meet the Candidates', whose Wyoming section lists the Constitution Party of Wyoming's candidates. Each of these candidates is on the November ballot under that party's own label, so a line adds nothing to the party printed on the ballot; the lists are kept whole for the record. Lines matched although the page spells the name differently from the ballot keep the page's spelling in 'as_listed' (Dudley Case for Manna Dudley Case, Susan E. Schmid for Suzie Schmid, Ken for Kenneth R. Casner, Donald for Don VanMatre, Ben-David for Ben David, and names without the middle initial the ballot prints). Albany County's 'WYOMNG STATE SENATE: Rothfuss' gives no district; Chris Rothfuss is the only candidate of that name for the Senate on the November list (District 9). Federal offices on these pages are outside this file. Read on 2026-10-02 with the kit's honest User-Agent, each site's robots.txt checked first; every page in 'lists' was opened a second time and a record is kept only if the page still showed it (none was lost). Facebook pages are social media and were not read. What could not be read is under 'not_read', each with the reason; the Wyoming Republican Party's own pages are the main gap (see there). One thing for a person to look at: the Constitution Party's page lists Tony Perry and Cheryl Hulme for 'State Senate', District 10 and District 15, while the Secretary of State's November list has both as the party's candidates for State Representative in those district numbers; they are left unmatched rather than guessed.

not_read.why: not read. The party's site (wyoming.gop) sends every page as the same empty shell and loads the text by script from its /api/ path, which the site's robots.txt asks programs not to read; the pages themselves are allowed but hold no text (also tried for /candidates, /news/wygop-supports-homeowner-property-tax-initiative-and-candidate-campaigns and /news/chairmans-letter-united-for-november-2026). News reports say the party's State Central Committee endorsed Brent Bien (Governor), Rachel Rodriguez-Williams (Secretary of State), Scott Smith (Treasurer) and Tom Kelly (Superintendent) before the August 18 primary; all four lost that primary (the database's primary lists show them as 'lost'), and nothing is recorded from news reports. Reading the /api/ path, or the pages in a browser, is John's decision.
read (its sitemaps); the domain no longer belongs to the party (its posts since 2024 are unrelated advertising), so nothing there is used
held, not read: the site's robots.txt asks every program to stay out (Disallow: /), so nothing on it was opened; whether it lists 2026 candidates is not known

not read: the address did not answer with a certificate for its own name, and later did not resolve; news reports describe the unit's first endorsements, made before the August primary, but no page of the party's own showing them was found

the state party's county directory is part of the same script-loaded site and could not be read; searches found no other county Republican page listing 2026 endorsements (Goshen County's party said publicly it did not take part in endorsing)

not read: the site answers with a self-signed certificate, and certificate checking is never turned off to get a page. News reports say its convention's nominations of Cale Case and Karlee Provenza were rejected by the Secretary of State; the four Libertarians on the November list (Ryan Shollenberger, Carrie Satterwhite, Holly M. Butler, Joseph Porambo) have no party page read here

not read: the address tried answered 503 (Service Unavailable) on both attempts, and no other site of the state party's own was found; its candidates are read from the national committee's page instead
read; its 2026 Candidates page names only the two federal candidates, which are outside this file
no site of their own listing 2026 candidates was found (the state party's list covers their counties)
